elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted operative sentence in Section 9: "Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor." The conformed § 2.1 ("without reduction rights but subject to Customer's termination rights") no longer negates it.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor" — 30 days, written, and no additional conditions or approvals attached.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Relied-on § 10.2 says only "Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination." A refund covering the post-termination period is not an express pro-rata refund, and the refund is narrowed to "recurring" Fees, so prepaid non-recurring/usage/professional-services Fees are not captured. The new § 9 convenience sentence adds no refund at all.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term." Retained §§ 9.1–9.3 give Vendor only for-cause and insolvency rights, so nothing contradicts it.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The drafted right runs on "thirty days' prior written notice," which is outside the 60–90 day band this fallback element specifies (more favourable to Customer, but literally not the fallback term).

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no early-termination fee, penalty, or accelerated-payment mechanic is imposed on Customer's convenience termination anywhere in the rendered text, so the cap has nothing to bite on and Customer exits fee-free.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply and is exceeded: Vendor is expressly given no convenience right at all during a committed term, and no other clause grants Vendor a no-cause exit.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Vendor has no convenience termination right to notice under the redlined Section 9.

reasons: Preferred level is incomplete on the refund element only. Repair in operative language by adding to the new Section 9 convenience sentence: "...in which case Vendor shall refund, on a pro-rata basis, all prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination." Do not rely on § 10.2: "prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination" is not expressly pro rata and excludes prepaid non-recurring Fees (implementation, professional services, usage prepayments).

Fallback level is also incomplete: the 30-day notice does not sit in the 60–90 day band. That is deliberate and Customer-favourable, so the fix is to complete the preferred level (add the pro-rata refund), not to lengthen notice.
Elements 1, 2 and 4 of the preferred checklist are cleanly met by the inserted Section 9 sentence, which follows the model language and correctly omits the surplus "in whole or in part."

Minimality holds: the only collateral edit is § 2.1, where deleting "or termination" and adding "subject to Customer's termination rights" is necessary to remove a retained sentence that would otherwise contradict the new right; the Customer-favourable "without reduction" restriction is preserved and no extras (survival tails, procedures, damages categories) are added.

Intent is preserved: for-cause, insolvency, security/SLA, Order-Form-severability and remedy-cumulation mechanics in §§ 9.1–9.3 and 9.5 survive unchanged, and no cross-reference is left dangling. Minor drafting hygiene: the inserted sentence is unnumbered (the document already skips 9.4) — number it 9.4 so later references have a hook.
